subject: Add a workflow to build PuTTYNG from a pinned PuTTY tag
body:
Add a workflow to build PuTTYNG from a pinned PuTTY tag

The bundled PuTTYNG.exe is 0.83. PuTTY 0.84 fixes a remotely triggerable
double-free in RSA key exchange, a remotely triggerable crash in NIST ECDSA
signature verification, and trust-sigil marking for Telnet/Rlogin after proxy
authentication. There is no upstream PuTTYNG 0.84: the last release is
v0.83.0.1.x64 from October 2025.

Stock putty.exe cannot be substituted. PuTTYNG is patched to take -hwndparent
and to draw no border so it can be hosted in a tab, and PuttyTypeDetector
changes mRemoteNG's behaviour based on the binary's InternalName.

Ports the patches from mRemoteNG/PuTTYNG's PuTTYNG.ps1 with two changes:

- Checks out an explicit tag. The original clones master and never checks out
  anything, so its output depends on the day it runs, while labelling the
  result with whatever tag git describe finds.
- Every anchor is verified and a miss is fatal. The original computes
  IndexOf() + .Length + 1 and then guards with
  ; when the anchor is missing IndexOf returns -1 and
  the guard still passes, so it edits at a meaningless offset. A silent miss
  would yield a PuTTYNG that pops modal dialogs behind the tab, or that ignores
  -hwndparent and cannot embed at all.

All five source anchors were checked against the 0.84 source before writing
this. Builds with the VS 2026 generator, since make22.cmd hardcodes VS 2022
paths that no longer exist on windows-latest.

The output is self-built and unsigned; the job summary reports the version
resource and SHA256 for review before it replaces the committed binary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
patch:
--- .github/workflows/Build_PuTTYNG.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,217 @@
+name: Build PuTTYNG
+
+# Builds the embedded SSH client from upstream PuTTY source.
+#
+# mRemoteNG ships PuTTYNG.exe, a patched PuTTY that accepts -hwndparent and draws no window
+# border so it can be hosted inside a tab. Stock putty.exe is not a substitute. The patches live
+# in mRemoteNG/PuTTYNG's PuTTYNG.ps1, which clones PuTTY's master and never checks out a tag, so
+# what it produces depends on the day it is run. This pins an explicit tag instead.
+#
+# The result is a self-built binary and is NOT signed or endorsed by upstream. Verify the version
+# resource in the job summary before committing it over mRemoteNG/PuTTYNG.exe.
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      putty_tag:
+        description: 'PuTTY git tag to build (e.g. 0.84)'
+        required: true
+        default: '0.84'
+
+jobs:
+  build-puttyng:
+    runs-on: windows-latest
+
+    steps:
+      - name: (01) Clone PuTTY at the requested tag
+        shell: pwsh
+        run: |
+          git clone https://git.tartarus.org/simon/putty.git putty
+          cd putty
+          git checkout "tags/${{ inputs.putty_tag }}"
+          Write-Host "HEAD is now: $(git describe --tags --always)" -ForegroundColor Green
+
+      # Ported from mRemoteNG/PuTTYNG's PuTTYNG.ps1, with one deliberate change: every anchor is
+      # verified before use and a miss is fatal.
+      #
+      # The original computes $startIndex = IndexOf($anchor) + $anchor.Length + 1 and then checks
+      # `if ($startIndex -ge 0)`. When the anchor is absent IndexOf returns -1, so $startIndex is
+      # still positive and the guard passes, and it edits at a meaningless offset. A patch that
+      # silently misses here would produce a PuTTYNG that pops modal dialogs behind a tab, or one
+      # that ignores -hwndparent and cannot be embedded at all.
+      - name: (02) Apply the mRemoteNG patches
+        shell: pwsh
+        run: |
+          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+          $tag = "${{ inputs.putty_tag }}"
+
+          function Assert-Anchor([string]$Content, [string]$Anchor, [string]$File) {
+            $count = ([regex]::Matches($Content, [regex]::Escape($Anchor))).Count
+            if ($count -ne 1) {
+              Write-Host "ERROR: expected exactly 1 occurrence of anchor in $File, found $count" -ForegroundColor Red
+              Write-Host "       anchor: $Anchor" -ForegroundColor Red
+              Write-Host "       PuTTY $tag has moved; the patch must be re-checked against this release." -ForegroundColor Red
+              exit 1
+            }
+          }
+
+          function Replace-Block([string]$File, [string]$StartAnchor, [string]$EndAnchor, [string]$NewBlock) {
+            $content = Get-Content -Path $File -Raw
+            Assert-Anchor $content $StartAnchor $File
+            Assert-Anchor $content $EndAnchor $File
+
+            $startIndex = $content.IndexOf($StartAnchor) + $StartAnchor.Length + 1
+            $endIndex = $content.IndexOf($EndAnchor, $startIndex)
+            if ($endIndex -lt $startIndex) {
+              Write-Host "ERROR: end anchor precedes start anchor in $File" -ForegroundColor Red
+              exit 1
+            }
+
+            $modified = $content.Remove($startIndex, $endIndex - $startIndex).Insert($startIndex, $NewBlock)
+            Set-Content -Path $File -Value $modified
+            Write-Host "Patched block in $File" -ForegroundColor Green
+          }
+
+          # --- cmdline.c: accept -hwndparent (embedding) and -auth-plugin ---
+          $workFile = "putty\cmdline.c"
+          $anchor = 'if (!strcmp(p, "-load")) {'
+          Assert-Anchor (Get-Content $workFile -Raw) $anchor $workFile
+          $newContent = '
+          #ifdef PUTTYNG
+              if (!stricmp(p, "-hwndparent")) {
+                  RETURN(2);
+                  hwnd_parent = atoi(value);
+                  return 2;
+              }
+              if (!strcmp(p, "-auth-plugin") || !strcmp(p, "-auth_plugin")) {
+                  RETURN(2);
+                  UNAVAILABLE_IN(TOOLTYPE_NONNETWORK);
+                  SAVEABLE(0);
+                  conf_set_str(conf, CONF_auth_plugin, value);
+                  return 2;
+              }
+          #endif
+
+              if (!strcmp(p, "-load")) {'
+          (Get-Content $workFile).Replace($anchor, $newContent) | Set-Content $workFile
+          Write-Host "Patched $workFile" -ForegroundColor Green
+
+          # --- putty.h: hwnd_parent, and always report maximised so no border is drawn ---
+          $workFile = "putty\putty.h"
+          $anchor = 'extern const char *const appname;'
+          Assert-Anchor (Get-Content $workFile -Raw) $anchor $workFile
+          $newContent = 'extern const char *const appname;
+
+          #ifdef PUTTYNG
+          int hwnd_parent;
+          #define IsZoomed(hWnd) TRUE
+          #endif // PUTTYNG'
+          (Get-Content $workFile).Replace($anchor, $newContent) | Set-Content $workFile
+          Write-Host "Patched $workFile" -ForegroundColor Green
+
+          # --- version.h: stamp the build. A git checkout carries placeholders; the release
+          #     tarball does not, which is why this builds from git rather than the tarball. ---
+          $workFile = "putty\version.h"
+          $content = Get-Content $workFile -Raw
+          Assert-Anchor $content 'Unidentified build' $workFile
+          Assert-Anchor $content '-Unidentified-Local-Build' $workFile
+          Assert-Anchor $content '0,0,0,0' $workFile
+          $setNewVersion = $tag.split(".")[0] + "," + $tag.split(".")[1] + ",0,1"
+          (Get-Content $workFile).Replace('Unidentified build', 'Release ' + $tag + ' mRemoteNG') | Set-Content $workFile
+          (Get-Content $workFile).Replace('-Unidentified-Local-Build', '-Release-mRemoteNG-Build') | Set-Content $workFile
+          (Get-Content $workFile).Replace('0,0,0,0', $setNewVersion) | Set-Content $workFile
+          Write-Host "Patched $workFile -> Release $tag mRemoteNG ($setNewVersion)" -ForegroundColor Green
+
+          # --- window.c: report errors into the terminal instead of a modal MessageBox, which
+          #     would otherwise appear detached from the tab hosting the session ---
+          Replace-Block "putty\windows\window.c" `
+            'char *title = dupprintf("%s Fatal Error", appname);' `
+            'if (conf_get_int(wgs->conf, CONF_close_on_exit) == FORCE_ON)' `
+            '    win_seat_output(seat,true,"\r\n\r\n",4);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,"------------------- ",20);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,title,strlen(title));
+              win_seat_output(seat,0," ------------------\r\n",22);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,"- ",2);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,msg,strlen(msg));
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,"\r\n\r\n",4);
+              sfree(title);
+
+              '
+
+          Replace-Block "putty\windows\window.c" `
+            'char *title = dupprintf("%s Error", appname);' `
+            'sfree(title);' `
+            '    win_seat_output(seat,true,"\r\n\r\n",4);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,"------------------- ",20);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,title,strlen(title));
+              win_seat_output(seat,0," ------------------\r\n",22);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,"- ",2);
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,msg,strlen(msg));
+              win_seat_output(seat,0,"\r\n\r\n",4);
+              '
+
+      # make22.cmd in the PuTTYNG repo hardcodes Visual Studio 2022 paths and the
+      # "Visual Studio 17 2022" generator. windows-latest is now the VS 2026 image, so that script
+      # cannot run here; cmake is left to pick the newest generator it finds instead.
+      - name: (03) Build
+        shell: pwsh
+        run: |
+          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+          cd putty
+          # PUTTYNG gates the -hwndparent and IsZoomed patches above. Without it the binary builds
+          # but cannot be embedded, which is not something to discover at runtime.
+          cmake -B build -A x64 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="/DPUTTYNG"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
+          cmake --build build --config Release --target putty
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
+
+      - name: (04) Verify and stage the binary
+        shell: pwsh
+        run: |
+          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+          $built = "putty\build\Release\putty.exe"
+          if (-not (Test-Path $built)) {
+            Write-Host "ERROR: putty.exe was not produced" -ForegroundColor Red
+            Get-ChildItem putty\build -Recurse -Filter "*.exe" | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName
+            exit 1
+          }
+
+          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path artifact | Out-Null
+          Copy-Item $built "artifact\PuTTYNG.exe"
+
+          $vi = (Get-Item "artifact\PuTTYNG.exe").VersionInfo
+          $hash = (Get-FileHash "artifact\PuTTYNG.exe" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
+
+          # mRemoteNG's PuttyTypeDetector keys off InternalName containing "PuTTYNG", and treats a
+          # plain PuTTY differently (it starts it minimised and expects window borders). A binary
+          # that failed this check would be mis-detected at runtime rather than at build time.
+          if ($vi.ProductVersion -notmatch 'mRemoteNG') {
+            Write-Host "ERROR: version resource does not identify an mRemoteNG build: $($vi.ProductVersion)" -ForegroundColor Red
+            exit 1
+          }
+
+          $summary = @"
+          ## PuTTYNG build
+
+          | Field | Value |
+          |---|---|
+          | PuTTY tag | ``${{ inputs.putty_tag }}`` |
+          | FileVersion | ``$($vi.FileVersion)`` |
+          | ProductVersion | ``$($vi.ProductVersion)`` |
+          | InternalName | ``$($vi.InternalName)`` |
+          | SHA256 | ``$hash`` |
+
+          Self-built and unsigned. Replaces ``mRemoteNG/PuTTYNG.exe`` only after review.
+          "@
+          $summary | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY -Append -Encoding utf8
+
+          Write-Host "FileVersion:    $($vi.FileVersion)" -ForegroundColor Green
+          Write-Host "ProductVersion: $($vi.ProductVersion)" -ForegroundColor Green
+          Write-Host "SHA256:         $hash" -ForegroundColor Green
+
+      - name: (05) Upload PuTTYNG.exe
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
+        with:
+          name: PuTTYNG-${{ inputs.putty_tag }}-x64
+          path: artifact/PuTTYNG.exe
+          retention-days: 7

security_flags.reason: CI workflow changes are the primary supply-chain vector (pull_request_target abuse, workflow injection)

triage.rationale: Pinned, anchor-verified PuTTYNG build workflow (dispatch-only) improves supply-chain reproducibility of shipped PuTTYNG.exe; standalone file, no conflict with our CI.

votes.concern: Produced binary keeps InternalName=PuTTY, so this fork will not recognize it as PuTTYNG despite the workflow’s misleading green verification.
votes.reason: Updating PuTTY is valuable, but this workflow breaks the fork’s detection contract and also interpolates untrusted input into PowerShell.

votes.concern: Future upstream PuTTY source changes might break regex patches, but the workflow's strict assertion checks prevent silent failures.
votes.reason: Provides a secure, reproducible, and pinned PuTTYNG build process with strict patch verification, crucial for upgrading to PuTTY 0.84.

votes.concern: Embedded patches may not match this fork; unsigned binary still needs human vetting.
votes.reason: Useful pinned PuTTYNG build CI for SSH stability, but patch parity and binary drop need maintainer judgment.

dissent: codex: REJECT - Updating PuTTY is valuable, but this workflow breaks the fork’s detection contract and also interpolates untrusted input into PowerShell.
grok: NEEDS_HUMAN - Useful pinned PuTTYNG build CI for SSH stability, but patch parity and binary drop need maintainer judgment.
